## ⚠️ The finding that reframes everything

**The worktree I was handed was NOT based on `034ac07936`.** It was cut from `origin/main` (`68cb75479a`) — `git merge-base --is-ancestor 034ac07936 HEAD` → **false**. Every file/line reference in the mission (`stream_constants.rs:79-81`, `:54`, `:167,181,198-200`, `streams.rs:2191-2197`, `DefaultSpec::Int(1)`, `BUILTIN_FILTER_NAMES`) matched the **streams branch**, which is how I caught it. I did the work on both bases:

| branch | HEAD | base | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`clf-streams-filters`** | **`c5b18ba0a6`** | **`034ac07936`** ✅ | **the mission, all 7 items** |
| `worktree-agent-a70e7663fda8f8e62` | `53b069d2f9` | `origin/main` | same defects as they exist on main (secondary — will conflict when the streams branch merges) |

Worktree `…/worktrees/agent-a70e7663fda8f8e62`; nothing pushed; tree clean; no `.codebase-memory` staged.

## Before → after, measured (streams branch)

| # | before | after (= `php -n` 8.5.6) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CONNECT/PERSISTENT/ASYNC_CONNECT` = `1,2,4`; catalog `flags` default `Int(1)` | `4,1,2`; default `Int(4)`. **No internal reader** — `lower_stream_socket_client` never reads operand 4 |
| 2 | `strip_tags` attach → `resource(6)`, `<p>Hello <b>World</b></p>` → `Hello World` | `Warning: … Unable to locate filter "string.strip_tags"` + `false`, bytes untouched; both state machines deleted |
| 3 | `stream_filter_append($m,"string.toupper",0)` → `abc` | `ABC`; full matrix `ABC\|ABC\|ABC\|ABC\|abc\|ABC` + `XYZ\|XYZ\|xyz\|XYZ` **identical to php**; catalog → `filter_name`/`mode`, default `0` |
| 4 | `consumed` → warning + `false` | resource + pass-through (`hel`/`lo `/`abcdef`) |
| 5 | — | **refused, documented** |
| 6 | 11 wrappers in elephc order; 14 concrete filters | php's registration order; php's 9 families |
| 7 | 5 php-src-internal constants declared | removed |

**Item 3's key design call**: the helper reads the recorded **mode string** off the stream state, not `fcntl(F_GETFL)` — the latter collapses `a` into `w`, the exact distinction php's rule tests. Guard is `mode & 3`, matching php's `(read_write & PHP_STREAM_FILTER_ALL) == 0`.
**Item 4**: id **13** — `__rt_fwrite` claims 4/10/12, and an unclaimed id is left byte-for-byte alone, which *is* php's `consumed`. Zero new asm.
**Item 5 refused**: a resolved id becomes a chain node, and the chain hands ids to `__rt_apply_stream_filter`, a *byte transform*. zlib/bzip2/iconv are per-call-site attach sequences with per-fd handles and program-local thunks — adding them would mint a node that **reports success and filters nothing**, worse than the refusal.

## Tests corrected *with* a measurement (they pinned the defects)

`stream_client_connect_is_one` (asserted `1`) → `stream_client_flags_match_php_src_order` + 2 new invariant tests · `test_stream_filter_strip_tags_removes_html` (asserted `"Hello World"`) → `…_is_not_a_php_filter` · the two list tests · the eval and magician introspection tests. Each carries php's output and its own previous expectation. Four new tests added.
